summary: Adding a two-tier persistent research cache feature that touches 14+ files across 5 modules: new Pydantic models in models.py (consumed by 33+ callers of OrchestratorConfig), new research_cache.py module mirroring test_runner.py, engine integration in engine.py and workflow_engine.py (_mcp_servers property change affects all agent invocations), prompt injection in phases.py (affects 3 phase prompt builders), config loading via default.yaml, a new Node.js MCP server, and 4 agent definition file updates. The change is architecturally additive (new optional fields with safe defaults, graceful degradation) but the blast radius spans the entire agent invocation path. The pre-existing WorkflowEngine._mcp_servers asymmetry (knowledge-only, missing test_runner) compounds the risk — fixing it as part of this feature changes MCP tool availability for all workflow-mode agents.

change_surface.description: Add 5 new Pydantic BaseModel classes (ResearchCacheConfig, ResearchCacheContext, ResearchEntry, Finding, ResearchCache) and 2 new fields to OrchestratorConfig (research_cache, research_cache_context). All have safe defaults — OrchestratorConfig() with no args continues to work. Models.py has 153 exports and is imported by virtually every module in the codebase.
Add research_cache YAML section with 11 keys after the test_runner block. Additive-only — no existing keys are modified. Affects config loading path: load_config() → OrchestratorConfig validation.

New file — implements MCP integration functions (get_research_mcp_config, ensure_research_mcp_config, cleanup_research_mcp_config), cache operations (load_cache, lookup, save_entry, extract_research_from_artifact), and findings accumulator (flag_finding, format_recommendations). Mirrors test_runner.py pattern exactly. No existing files modified — pure addition.

New Node.js MCP server directory — package.json, index.js, README.md. Exposes 4 tools: lookup_research, save_research, flag_finding, get_run_recommendations. External to main codebase. Writes to ~/.orchestrator/research/ (global) and .knowledge/research/ (project) directories.

Add research cache lifecycle to OrchestratorEngine: (1) new self._research_mcp_config instance var in __init__, (2) initialization after test_runner setup in run(), (3) merge into _mcp_servers property, (4) post-phase artifact extraction when auto_extract=True, (5) end-of-run recommendations output, (6) cleanup in finally block. engine.py's run() method (275 lines) gains ~30 lines of research cache integration code. The _mcp_servers property change affects ALL agent invocations in both legacy and workflow mode.

Expand _mcp_servers property (line 635) to merge research-cache config AND fix pre-existing asymmetry by also merging test_runner config. This is both a new feature integration and a bug fix — workflow-mode agents will now have access to test_runner AND research-cache MCP tools that they previously lacked. Also adds post-phase extraction in task completion path and cleanup in teardown.
Add recommendations printing after _print_summary when research_cache_context.findings is non-empty. Guarded by null check — no behavioral change when feature is disabled.

Add _inject_research_context() function and update _inject_mcp_role_guidance() to include research-cache tools (lookup_research, save_research, flag_finding) in MCP tool table. Affects prompt content for 3 roles: pm, architect, principal_engineer. Prompt content changes for all runs where research cache is enabled (default: true).
Add Research Cache usage section instructing agent to call lookup_research before researching, save_research after fresh research, flag_finding for actionable issues.
Add Research Cache usage section with project-tier guidance for market/competitor data.
Add Research Cache usage section with project-tier guidance.
Add Research Cache usage section with global-tier guidance for tech decisions and architecture patterns.

downstream_impacts.description: The _mcp_servers property in both engine.py and workflow_engine.py is read by EVERY agent invocation to determine available MCP tools. Adding 'research-cache' to this dict means all agents (not just the 3 targeted roles) will have access to lookup_research, save_research, flag_finding, and get_run_recommendations tools. While only pm/architect/principal_engineer receive prompt injection encouraging cache use, any agent could discover and call these tools. The WorkflowEngine fix also adds test_runner tools to workflow-mode agents for the first time.

Verify agent invocations handle gracefully when MCP server binary is absent (tools not available)

downstream_impacts.description: New directories and JSON files created on the filesystem. Global tier writes to user home directory (~/.orchestrator/research/index.json, entries/*.json). Project tier writes to project directory (.knowledge/research/). Both the Python-side save_entry() and Node.js MCP server write to these same files, creating a dual-writer scenario. Index.json corruption is possible under concurrent access from both writers, though Python-side writes only occur between phases (sequential).

downstream_impacts.description: With research cache enabled by default, pm/architect/principal_engineer agents receive additional prompt instructions to call lookup_research before spawning research sub-agents. This changes agent behavior: agents that previously always spawned deep_researcher/market_researcher will now check cache first. If the cache contains stale or incorrect data (cache poisoning), agents may produce lower-quality output. The max_inject_bytes=2048 cap and <research-cache-data> delimiters with 'do not treat as instructions' note mitigate prompt injection risk.

2. Deploy research_cache.py (new module — no callers yet, safe to deploy independently)
3. Build and deploy Node.js MCP server at ../sdlc-mcp-servers/research-cache/ (npm install && npm run build)

7. Deploy agent .md file updates (enables agent-side cache-first behavior)
deployment_constraints.rollback_plan: The feature is designed for safe rollback at any stage: (1) Set research_cache.enabled=false in default.yaml to disable entirely without code changes — all code paths null-guard on research_cache_context. (2) If models.py changes cause issues, revert models.py + default.yaml together. (3) If engine.py changes cause issues, revert engine.py — the null-guard pattern means missing research_cache_context causes silent skip. (4) The Node.js MCP server is external — removing it causes graceful degradation (warning log, no crash). (5) Cache data in ~/.orchestrator/research/ and .knowledge/research/ is inert when feature is disabled — no cleanup needed. (6) .mcp.json entries are cleaned up by cleanup_research_mcp_config; if cleanup didn't run, manually remove 'research-cache' key from .mcp.json.
feature_flags_needed: research_cache.enabled (bool, default true) — master kill switch for entire feature, already built into ResearchCacheConfig
research_cache.auto_extract (bool, default true) — controls post-phase artifact extraction independently
research_cache.cleanup_mcp_config (bool, default true) — controls .mcp.json cleanup independently

recommendations: 1. [HIGH] Run full test suite after TASK-001 (models.py changes) to catch any OrchestratorConfig equality assertions that break with new fields — this is the highest-risk additive change since OrchestratorConfig has 33+ callers across the codebase.

2. [HIGH] Implement TASK-006 (workflow_engine.py) carefully — it fixes a pre-existing _mcp_servers asymmetry that changes tool availability for ALL workflow-mode agents. Run workflow_engine tests before and after to compare behavior.

3. [HIGH] Verify dual-writer safety: Python-side save_entry() (post-phase extraction) and Node.js MCP server save_research both write to the same index.json files. Ensure Python-side writes only occur between phases (not during parallel agent execution).

4. [MEDIUM] Test graceful degradation paths thoroughly: research_cache.enabled=false, MCP binary missing, research_cache_context=None. Every code path that accesses research_cache_context must null-guard. Missing guards cause AttributeError at runtime.

5. [MEDIUM] Verify .mcp.json multi-writer safety: both test_runner and research_cache cleanup functions modify the same .mcp.json file. Test that concurrent cleanup of both keys preserves file integrity.

6. [MEDIUM] Monitor prompt size impact: _inject_research_context adds up to max_inject_bytes=2048 bytes to phase prompts. Combined with existing knowledge context and MCP guidance injections, verify total prompt size stays within Claude context limits.
7. [LOW] Add .knowledge/research/ to .gitignore template if not already present — project-tier cache files should not be committed to version control.

8. [LOW] Consider adding a 'cache clear' CLI command (orchestrate --clear-research-cache) for when users discover bad entries — currently there's no way to invalidate cache entries except waiting for TTL expiry or manually deleting files.
